inputs.root_cause: GAP-020: xliff had no implementation-evidence ledger, so its 142 obligations had never been classified against source symbols or test selectors and neither the exact-obligation reconciler nor the proof-requirement audit could run for it.

execution_steps: 1. Read the register: 142 obligations across 15 capabilities.

2. Applied the GAP-018 namespace filter and confirmed the measurement: exactly ONE of xliff's 11 test files imports format_factory.xliff. The other ten import the deprecated xliff.* shadow package and cannot supply selectors.
3. Read that one file (test_production_namespace.py, 15 tests, 343 lines) and mapped its tests to capabilities by what they actually exercise, not by name similarity.

4. Four capabilities have no shipped-namespace test at all -- XLIFF-MODULE-001 (18 obligations), XLIFF-NOTE-001 (4), XLIFF-MERGE-001 (2), XLIFF-QA-001 (2). They are mapped with no tests so the builder records them `missing` with the reason, rather than being omitted.
5. Ran the full suite: 193 passed, no failures, so the declared result is a clean PASS -- unlike safetensors, xliff has no known environment failures.
6. Built the ledger and ran the proof-requirement audit over it.

evidence.suite_truth: 193 passed with no failures. That number is however dominated by the ten shadow-package files: the single shipped-namespace file contributes 15 tests. A green suite here says very little about the package that would be released, which is precisely what GAP-018 predicted.
evidence.obligations_moved_note: Zero. Mapping is not proving. Every entry is partial at most and none has completed its proof-requirement audit.
